h-sirr-zawj.n: The private life of a marriage is a trust; exposing it, even in anger or jest, is a betrayal.

h-arba-nifaq.n: A practical test for any relationship or partnership: trust, truthfulness, loyalty, and fairness in a dispute.

h-shiqq-tamra.n: Do not belittle the little you have: half a date, or a kind word, may be all someone needs today.

h-haqq-khams.n: Small duties that build bonds: a greeting, a visit to the sick, presence at a funeral. Their absence is what people feel as coldness.

h-khurfat-janna.n: Visiting the sick is not a courtesy: it is a harvest of Paradise for you and great comfort for them.

h-dua-marid.n: A short supplication said at a sick person's side, joining treatment with reliance on the Healer.

h-dua-abi-salama.n: The Prophet's prayer when Abu Salamah died; one can pray it for anyone lost, asking also for those left behind.

h-dam-al-ayn.n: Tears and grief over a loss carry no sin; what counts is what the tongue says in protest or resentment.

h-rahma-qulub.n: The Prophet said this with tears in his eyes: weeping at a loss is mercy, not weak faith.

h-dua-mayyit.n: One of the fullest prayers for the deceased; praying for them is among the best kindness after they are gone.

h-nafs-maddin.n: Debt reaches beyond this life; planning its repayment and writing it down is responsibility, not anxiety.

h-kullun-muyassar.n: Belief in decree is no reason to stop acting: act, trusting that the path meant for you will be made easy.

h-bayt-al-hamd.n: For a parent who has lost a child: Allah calls your child “the fruit of your heart”; He knows your pain and prepares a house for your patience.

h-kalimatan.n: An easy start when faith feels weak: words that take seconds yet weigh heavily.

h-audhu-jubn.n: Seeking refuge from cowardice, miserliness and frail old age; helpful for fear of confrontation or of the future.

h-aainni-dhikr.n: A cure for weak motivation: ask for help with worship itself rather than waiting to feel motivated.

h-dhanbi-kullah.n: For someone weighed down by countless sins: a prayer that gathers them all and asks forgiveness for them at once.

h-bayt-dhikr.n: A home where Allah is remembered is alive; a little daily remembrance changes the home and the heart.

h-zann-abdi.n: Thinking well of Allah is a cure for despair: He is as His servant thinks of Him, so do not shut the door of hope.

h-ratb-lisan.n: Practical advice for someone overloaded: a light worship that stays with you all day.

h-majalis-dhikr.n: Tranquility descends on good gatherings; good company is a remedy for loneliness and anxiety.

h-kalimat-tammat.n: A short evening remembrance that gives the heart security when afraid of harm.

h-fatir-samawat.n: Seeking refuge from the evil of one's own self; helps those troubled by negative inner talk or recurring whispers.

h-muawwidhat-sabah.n: A simple daily protection for those worried about envy, harm or intrusive thoughts; it takes a minute.

h-bismika-wadatu.n: The bedtime prayer entrusts the soul to Allah each night; it eases night anxiety and fear of death.

h-aslamtu-nafsi.n: Entrusting your affairs to Allah before sleep lifts the weight of pending decisions once you have done your part.

h-at-amana.n: A daily reminder of blessings we treat as ordinary; gratitude for them eases the feeling of lack.

h-rabbana-atina.n: The Prophet's most frequent prayer: there is no conflict between asking for good in this life and in the next.

h-huda-tuqa.n: Four needs that protect a person: guidance, piety, chastity before desire, and independence from people.

h-ighfir-warhamni.n: A short prayer gathering the needs of both worlds; suited to someone crowded by worries.

h-musarrif-qulub.n: Hearts change; the fear of one's state changing is met with prayer, not with anxiety.

h-jahd-bala.n: A comprehensive refuge from severe hardship, bad outcomes and others' gloating; for times of heavy pressure.

h-aslih-dini.n: A prayer for the soundness of faith, livelihood and final return together; helpful when unsure of life's direction.

h-ajz-kasal.n: It distinguishes inability from laziness; seeking refuge from both is the first step to moving.

h-zalamtu-nafsi.n: Taught to Abu Bakr: admitting one's failings is not only for sinners but the state of every believer.

h-sharr-ghina-faqr.n: Wealth and poverty each have their trial; seeking refuge from the evil of both keeps a balanced view of money.

h-munkarat-akhlaq.n: For someone fighting a bad trait or habit: prayer is part of the treatment, not a substitute for it.

h-sharr-sami.n: It names each gate of weakness; suited to someone treating an addiction of the eyes or of desire.

h-ju-khiyana.n: Hunger and betrayal: hardship of living and of conscience; asked together, since the first may push to the second.

h-sal-afiya.n: Well-being is among the greatest things to ask for; praying for it goes together with seeking treatment.

h-dua-bi-zahr-ghayb.n: A practical cure for envy and grudges: pray in secret for the person, and the angel prays the same for you.

h-jazak-allah.n: A sincere word of thanks keeps relationships alive; ingratitude begins with forgetting to say it.

h-la-tadu-ala-anfusikum.n: In a moment of anger at children or oneself, dangerous words can be said; hold back and pray for good instead.

h-dua-istijaba.n: For anyone who feels their prayers go unanswered: the answer may be a gift, or an evil turned away that you never see.

h-shibr-ard.n: Taking land or inheritance unjustly, even a little, is a grave wrong; rights do not lapse by silence.

h-ma-bayna-lahyayh.n: The tongue and desire are the two great gates of error; guarding them is the shortest road to safety.

h-kalima-la-yatabayyan.n: Before you write or post: one thoughtless word can destroy what cannot be rebuilt, especially online.

h-thumma-istaqim.n: A sentence that sums up the path: a clear direction, then steadiness on it day after day.

h-amsik-lisanak.n: In times of strife and quarrels: hold your tongue, turn to your home, and mend yourself.

h-dimaukum-haram.n: A person's life, wealth and honour are sacred; attacking someone's reputation is like attacking their property.

h-azfar-nuhas.n: A stark image of backbiting: whoever wounds others' honour ends up wounding himself.

h-radd-an-ird.n: When you hear backbiting in a gathering, defending the absent person is worship, not meddling.

h-adh.n: Carrying words between people ruins relationships more than the words themselves; stopping the chain with you is a virtue.

h-dhu-wajhayn.n: Pleasing everyone with two faces costs you everyone's respect; calm clarity is nobler than double flattery.

h-tahallum.n: Eavesdropping on people's talk or messages violates their privacy, even when driven by worry or jealousy.

h-kafa-kadhiban.n: Before you share: passing on everything you hear counts as lying even if you did not invent it.

h-mutashabbi.n: Pretending to a life or success you do not have, as often happens online, is a falsehood that wears out its owner first.

h-la-yanbaghi-lianan.n: Cursing creeps in during anger; a person true to himself keeps his tongue clean of it.

h-sibab-fusuq.n: Disagreement does not justify insults; a wounding word is a sin however wrong the other side is.

h-la-tasubbu-amwat.n: After death, the accounts between people close; there is no place for settling scores with the departed.

h-yuta-ilayh.n: A golden rule for relationships and work: treat people as you would love to be treated.

h-la-tabaghadu.n: Three days is the limit for shunning after a dispute; after that, repair begins, even if only with a greeting.

h-awrat-al-muslimin.n: Hunting for faults and constant surveillance corrupt relationships, at home, at work and among friends.

h-yahqir.n: Contempt is not an opinion but an evil in itself, whatever the gap in wealth, knowledge or status.

h-man-ghashshana.n: Hiding a defect in a sale or in work is cheating, even if no one notices.

h-khabbaba.n: Turning a spouse against their partner, whether by family or friends, is a grave sin, not advice.

h-liwa-ghadir.n: Betrayal may stay hidden in this life but will be exposed on the Day; you need not carry the worry that the betrayer escapes.

h-ajir-ajrah.n: Withholding a worker's wage is a wrong Allah Himself takes up: comfort for the wronged, a warning for employers.

h-halaka-nas.n: Pessimistic generalising about people, out of contempt or despair, harms the speaker first.

h-tahrish.n: Many marital and family quarrels are incitement by Satan; knowing this softens the dispute.

h-la-yatanaja.n: Caring for someone who may feel left out is prophetic courtesy, in gatherings, groups and online.

h-hirra.n: Mercy to animals is part of faith; confining or neglecting an animal is a wrong one will answer for.

h-yuadhdhibuna-nas.n: Abuse is not a fate to be endured in the name of patience; Allah threatens those who torment people, and the victim may protect themselves.

h-aghna-shuraka.n: A deed done for people's eyes loses its worth; sincerity frees you from waiting for their approval.

h-sammaa.n: Displaying good deeds to be admired turns against its owner; keep some deeds hidden between you and Allah.

h-zina-ayn.n: Desire begins with small steps: a look, listening, talk; the cure is to cut the road at its start, not its end.

h-haqq-tariq.n: The rights of the road and public space: lowering the gaze and not causing harm; manners that protect everyone.

h-darb-khudud.n: Grief is legitimate, but self-harm and loud protest deepen the pain rather than ease it.

h-yujibuni-fal.n: Pessimism about days, numbers or objects has no basis; calm optimism is the Prophet's way.

h-iqtataa-haqq.n: Taking someone's rights with a false oath, in court, inheritance or business, is among the gravest wrongs.

h-kabair.n: Disobedience to parents is listed beside polytheism and murder, showing how heavy it is to wrong them.

h-fa-ti-khayr.n: You are not a prisoner of words said in anger or under pressure; if something better becomes clear, return to it and make amends.

h-la-tasubbi-humma.n: Illness is not necessarily punishment; it purifies, and feeling burdened by it does not mean weak faith.

h-fuhsh-haya.n: Obscene speech disfigures the finest relationship; modesty adorns the simplest.

h-laqisat-nafsi.n: Watch your inner talk: describing a bad state in harsh words makes it heavier.

h-yazim-masala.n: Pray with certainty and persistence, not hesitation; Allah is generous and asking does not burden Him.

h-ihdad.n: Mourning has a set limit; sadness remains in the heart, but life resumes afterwards.

h-la-yakhtub.n: Respect others' rights in proposals, work and trade; do not build your chance on wrecking someone else's.

h-qila-wa-qal.n: “It was said and he said” and wasting money: an exact diagnosis of much of what consumes our time today.

h-ahsibu.n: Excessive praise harms both the one who praises and the one praised; praise in measure and truthfully.

h-taun.n: A prophetic principle for epidemics: prevention and not spreading infection, with trust in Allah rather than panic.

h-wussida-amr.n: Putting the unqualified in charge is ruin; integrity in hiring and promotion is worship.

h-idha-lam-tastahi.n: When shame is gone, no limit remains; guard your modesty before Allah and people, offline and online.

h-liqa-allah.n: Disliking death is human; the believer, at its moment, is given news of mercy that makes the meeting beloved.

h-majra-dam.n: The Prophet said this to two men who saw him with his wife at night: clarifying early stops suspicion before it grows.

h-ijtihad-ajran.n: Whoever strives and errs is rewarded, not blamed: a cure for fear of deciding and for self-punishment after a mistake.

h-yughan.n: Even the Prophet's heart felt a veil needing forgiveness; low states are human and are treated, not despaired of.

h-law-lam-tudhnibu.n: Sin does not put you outside Allah's mercy; what matters is returning. This hadith breaks the sinner's despair.

h-rabbi-ighfir-li.n: The Prophet repeated it a hundred times in one sitting: seeking forgiveness is a daily habit, not an emergency.

h-astaghfiru-hayy.r: Zayd, the freed servant of the Prophet ﷺ
h-astaghfiru-hayy.n: No sin is greater than Allah's forgiveness; sincere seeking of pardon erases even grave sins.

h-ma-la-ayn-raat.n: For someone worn out by patience: what awaits you is beyond imagining, which gives suffering meaning.

h-tasihhu-la-tasqamu.n: For those tired of illness or loss: there is health with no illness after it, and meeting with no parting.

h-hamma-bi-hasana.n: Bad thoughts you refrain from acting on are written as good deeds; reassuring for those burdened by intrusive thoughts.

h-afrah-bi-tawba.n: Allah rejoices at your return; do not hold back from repenting out of shame at many sins.

h-ma-lam-yugharghir.n: The door of repentance stays open as long as there is breath; there is no “too late”.

h-wadiyan-min-dhahab.n: Greed is never satisfied; contentment comes not from more money but from a content heart.

h-lillahi-ma-akhadh.n: The Prophet's words to his daughter as her child was dying: consolation joining acceptance and patience.

h-safiyyuhu.n: Losing a beloved person is a great wound; the reward for patience over it is Paradise, nothing less.

h-ighfir-li-qawmi.n: The Prophet told of a prophet struck by his people: praying for those who hurt you is the highest level of forgiveness, not its obligation.

h-rahima-musa.n: When accused unfairly of injustice, remembering the patience of those before you eases the wound and prevents an outburst.

h-ajjala-uquba.n: Some of what befalls you in this life is relief, not punishment; do not read every hardship as anger.

h-bala-mumin.n: Trials in oneself, children and wealth are no sign of distance from Allah; they may be the path of purification.

h-athara.n: When facing favouritism at work or in society: do your duty well, seek your right through legitimate means, and pray.

h-isbiru-hatta-talqawni.n: Patience with favouritism and social injustice does not mean approving it, but not abandoning principles because of it.

h-la-tatamannaw-aduww.n: Do not seek confrontation; ask Allah for well-being, and if it comes, stand firm calmly.

h-tarkuhu-ma-la-yanih.n: Much anxiety comes from occupying ourselves with what does not concern us: news, others' lives, social media.

h-thalithuhuma.n: Said in the cave with danger close: Allah's company calms the heart when fear is at its height.

h-bismillah-tawakkaltu.n: A short remembrance on leaving home, calming for those anxious about the day or the road.

h-man-ada-li-waliyya.n: The road to Allah's love starts with the obligations, then small consistent voluntary acts, not one great leap.

h-shibran-dhiraa.n: A small step from you toward Allah is met with a greater nearness from Him; start with what you can.

h-abdan-shakura.n: Worship is gratitude before it is asking; thankfulness is lived through deeds, not words alone.

h-huffat-janna.n: The easy road is not always the right one; difficulty in doing good does not mean you are on the wrong path.

h-shirak-nalih.n: A small deed today may bring you very near Paradise, and a small word may take you far; belittle nothing.

h-tala-umruhu.n: A long life is a blessing when filled with good; what matters is what fills your years, not only their number.

h-firsin-shat.n: A small gift between neighbours builds warmth; do not hold back because it is little.

h-yaghrisu-gharsan.n: Beneficial work keeps rewarding you after you; even what is taken from you unjustly counts for you.

h-bima-tutiqun.n: Moderation in worship and work protects from burnout; a little that lasts is better than much that stops.

h-yusalli-nashatahu.n: Resting when tired is not negligence; the Prophet commanded it even in worship.

h-sanna-sunna.n: Taking the initiative in good multiplies its effects; be the first to start a good habit in your family or workplace.

h-dalla-ala-khayr.n: Sincere advice or a useful idea for someone else can be an ongoing charity.

h-safina.n: Silence about a wrong that harms everyone is not neutrality; family, work and society share one fate.

h-kalimat-adl.n: Speaking the truth respectfully to someone in power is great courage, weighed with care for consequences and safety.

h-akhadhu-ala-yadayh.n: Letting a wrongdoer carry on harms everyone; stopping him by the means available is a shared duty.

h-tuaddunna-huquq.n: For someone wronged without redress: nothing is lost; this eases the urge for revenge and gives patience meaning.

h-fal-yatahallalhu.n: Repenting from wronging people needs a step toward them, an apology or returning a right; today is easier than tomorrow.

h-illa-ddayn.n: Debt is a right of people that is not dropped even for a martyr; take care to record and repay it.

h-alhanu-bi-hujjatih.n: Winning an argument or a case through eloquence does not make wrong right; an outward verdict does not clear the conscience.

h-bunyan.n: Mutual support is what makes everyone stronger; you are not alone in your crisis.

h-akhu-al-muslim.n: The ethics of brotherhood: do not wrong or abandon, meet needs, cover faults; the reward matches the deed.

h-taqwa-hahuna.n: “Piety is here”, pointing to his chest: do not judge people by appearances or look down on anyone.

h-unsur-akhak.n: Loyalty to a friend or relative does not mean siding with their wrongdoing; holding them back is real support.

h-satara-abdan.n: Covering people's faults, not exposing them, is a way to Allah covering yours.

h-kullu-daif.n: A person's worth with Allah is not in strength or appearance; arrogance is the real loss.

h-khayrun-min-mil.n: Society measures people by money and status; the true measure lies elsewhere.

h-ashath-aghbar.n: Do not measure your worth by the doors that open for you; many rejected by people are accepted by Allah.

h-laallaka-aghdabtahum.n: Said to Abu Bakr about poor Companions: apologising to those we hurt is due, whatever our standing.

h-kafil-yatim-lahu.n: Caring for an orphan is among the deeds closest to the Prophet's company in Paradise.

h-yataffaf.n: Many in need do not ask, guarding their dignity; look for them and help them gently.

h-jariyatayn.n: Raising and caring for daughters is a great door of reward, not a burden.

h-bi-duafaikum.n: The weak and simple are a cause of good in society; do not look down on anyone.

h-haqq-zawja.n: Clear rights of a wife: provision, clothing and respect; insults and humiliation are not part of the religion.

h-dinar-ala-ahlik.n: Spending on one's family is not an ordinary burden; it is the greatest charity in reward.

h-yahbisa-qutah.n: Depriving one's family of maintenance, as punishment or out of stinginess, is a serious sin.

h-malakan.n: Giving does not reduce provision; a replacement comes with it.

h-yastafif.n: Refraining from asking and striving for self-sufficiency open the door of provision; start with your dependants.

h-maraqa.n: Sharing with neighbours, even a little, builds closeness; it does not need a big table.

h-khayr-ashab.n: The worth of friendship and neighbourliness lies in what you give, not in what you wait to receive.

h-rahim-maqam.n: Keeping family ties is promised Allah's connection; even a small step toward an estranged relative weighs much.

h-abulluha.n: You can differ with relatives in faith or outlook and still keep ties with them kindly; connection is not agreement.

h-awsat-abwab.n: Kindness to parents is an open gate to Paradise while they live; each day is a chance.

h-yasubbu-aba-rajul.n: Insulting someone's family comes back on your own; quarrels that touch mothers and fathers are graver than they seem.

h-wudd-abih.n: Kindness to a father after his death is possible: keep ties with his friends and those he loved.

h-kanat-wa-kanat.n: The Prophet's loyalty to Khadijah after her death: true love remains after loss and does not discredit the life that follows.

h-tibta.n: Visiting a friend or a sick person for Allah's sake is great in Allah's scales, however simple it looks.

h-la-tusahib.n: Friends shape you; choose company that helps you toward good.

h-arwah-junud.n: Not clicking with some people is no flaw in you or them; souls connect or differ.

h-halawat-iman.n: The sweetness of faith is tasted through sincere love; for anyone who has lost the taste of worship, start with the heart.

h-mutahabbun.n: Friendship for Allah's sake, without self-interest, has a great place with Allah.

h-qurab-al-ard.n: However many your sins, Allah's forgiveness is wider; do not let the past stop you from returning.

h-arhamu-biibadihi.n: Allah's mercy to you is greater than a mother's to her child: an image that breaks despair and dread of Allah.

h-mia-rahma.n: All the mercy you see among people is one part of a hundred; imagine Allah's mercy toward you.

h-law-yalamu-mumin.n: The balance of fear and hope: no false security that breeds carelessness, and no despair that shuts the door.

h-ma-al-faqr-akhsha.n: Competing for worldly things and constant comparison are more dangerous than poverty itself.

h-tais-abd-dinar.n: When your contentment depends on what you own, you become its slave; freedom lies in contentment.

h-mali-mali.n: What you truly own is what you used and what you gave; the rest you leave behind.

h-dhiban-jaian.n: Greed for money and position quietly devours principles; watch your motives.

h-ka-rakib.n: The world is a stop on the way; this view lightens attachment and the fear of loss.

h-la-tulam-ala-kafaf.n: You are not blamed if your income barely suffices; start with your family, then give from the surplus.

h-ayshuhu-kafafan.n: Happiness is not in more but in enough, with contentment.

h-thuluth.n: Moderation in eating is a prophetic health principle; useful for overeating or emotional eating.

h-bi-sakhawat-nafs.n: Blessing in money comes from how it is taken, not from how much.

h-anzalaha-billah.n: In financial hardship: begin with prayer and turning to Allah, alongside legitimate means.

h-tutimu-taam.n: Greeting strangers and feeding people break loneliness, theirs and yours.

h-adl-tamra.n: A small charity from lawful earnings grows with Allah; do not be shy of giving little.

h-la-hasad-illa.n: Healthy aspiration: wishing for the good another has, without wishing it taken from them.

h-la-yatamanna-mawt.n: For someone wishing for death out of pain: the Prophet forbade it because your staying holds good you have not yet seen. If the pain is heavy, reach out now to someone you trust or a professional.

h-husn-khuluq-saim.n: Good character with people is great worship; it may take you where fasting and night prayer would.

h-hilm-anah.n: Forbearance and deliberateness are loved by Allah; they cure outbursts and rushed decisions.

h-yuhram-rifq.n: Harshness in parenting, marriage or work deprives you of the very good you seek through it.

h-hayyin-layyin.n: Being easy to deal with is not weakness; it is the trait of those Allah has forbidden the Fire.

h-munaffirin.n: Harshness in religion and leadership drives people away; mercy to the weak is the Prophet's way.

h-man-waliya.n: Every person in charge, manager, parent or teacher, is treated as they treat those under them.

h-ihtajaba.n: The official who shuts his door to people's needs shuts the door of help on himself.

h-muqsitun.n: Justice begins at home, among children and spouses, then at work and in positions of responsibility.

h-la-taa-fi-masiya.n: Obeying a manager or authority is due in what is right; it ends at being ordered to sin or wrong others.

h-la-tasal-imara.n: Responsibility is heavy; do not seek it for status, and if it comes, seek Allah's help with it.

h-innaha-amana.n: Knowing your limits is not weakness; declining a responsibility you cannot carry is integrity and honesty with yourself.

h-bitanatan.n: Watch your inner circle; a good adviser is a blessing, a bad one drags you slowly.

te.lib:h-sirr-zawj: Among the worst of people in rank before Allah on the Day of Resurrection is the man who is intimate with his wife and she with him, and then he spreads her secret.
te.lib:h-arba-nifaq: Four traits, whoever has them all is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a trait of hypocrisy until he leaves it: when trusted he betrays, when he speaks he lies, when he makes a pact he breaks it, and when he quarrels he is outrageous.
te.lib:h-shiqq-tamra: Guard yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date; and whoever cannot find it, then with a good word.
te.lib:h-haqq-khams: The rights of a Muslim over a Muslim are five: returning the greeting, visiting the sick, following funerals, accepting invitations, and responding to one who sneezes.
te.lib:h-khurfat-janna: When a Muslim visits his sick brother, he remains in the harvest of Paradise until he returns.
te.lib:h-dua-marid: Whoever visits a sick person whose time has not come and says seven times beside him: “I ask Allah the Mighty, Lord of the Mighty Throne, to heal you”, Allah will heal him of that illness.
te.lib:h-dua-abi-salama: O Allah, forgive Abu Salamah, raise his rank among the guided, be the successor to those he left behind, forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds, make his grave spacious and give him light in it.
te.lib:h-dam-al-ayn: Do you not hear? Allah does not punish for the tears of the eye nor for the grief of the heart, but He punishes or shows mercy because of this (and he pointed to his tongue).
te.lib:h-rahma-qulub: This is a mercy that Allah has placed in the hearts of His servants; and Allah has mercy only on the merciful among His servants.
te.lib:h-dua-mayyit: O Allah, forgive him, have mercy on him, keep him safe and pardon him; honour his arrival, widen his entry, wash him with water, snow and hail, and cleanse him of sins as a white garment is cleansed of dirt; give him a home better than his home and family better than his family, admit him to Paradise and protect him from the punishment of the grave and of the Fire.
te.lib:h-nafs-maddin: The believer's soul is held by his debt until it is paid on his behalf.
te.lib:h-kullun-muyassar: Act, for everyone is eased toward what he was created for.
te.lib:h-bayt-al-hamd: When a servant's child dies, Allah says to His angels: “Did you take the child of My servant?” They say yes. He says: “Did you take the fruit of his heart?” They say yes. He says: “What did My servant say?” They say: “He praised You and said ‘To Allah we belong and to Him we return.’” Allah says: “Build for My servant a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.”
te.lib:h-kalimatan: Two words light on the tongue, heavy in the Balance, beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to Allah and praise Him; glory be to Allah the Magnificent.
te.lib:h-audhu-jubn: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness, I seek refuge in You from cowardice, I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most feeble age, I seek refuge in You from the trial of this world (meaning the trial of the Antichrist), and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave.
te.lib:h-aainni-dhikr: Mu‘adh, I advise you never to leave saying after every prayer: “O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You well.”
te.lib:h-dhanbi-kullah: O Allah, forgive me all my sins, the small and the great, the first and the last, the open and the secret.
te.lib:h-bayt-dhikr: The likeness of the house in which Allah is remembered and the house in which He is not remembered is that of the living and the dead.
te.lib:h-zann-abdi: Allah says: “I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it.”
te.lib:h-ratb-lisan: Keep your tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah.
te.lib:h-majalis-dhikr: No people sit remembering Allah but the angels surround them, mercy covers them, tranquility descends upon them, and Allah mentions them among those with Him.
te.lib:h-kalimat-tammat: Had you said in the evening, “I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He created”, it would not have harmed you.
te.lib:h-fatir-samawat: O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that there is no god but You; I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul and from the evil of Satan and his call to associate others with You.
te.lib:h-muawwidhat-sabah: Recite “Say: He is Allah, One” and the two chapters of refuge in the evening and the morning, three times; they will suffice you against everything.
te.lib:h-bismika-wadatu: When one of you goes to bed, let him dust off his bed with the inside of his garment, for he does not know what came onto it after him; then let him say: “In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side and by You I raise it; if You take my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, protect it as You protect Your righteous servants.”
te.lib:h-aslamtu-nafsi: When you go to bed, perform ablution as for prayer, lie on your right side and say: “O Allah, I submit myself to You, turn my face to You, entrust my affair to You and lean my back on You, in hope and in awe of You; there is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You revealed and in Your Prophet whom You sent.” If you die, you die upon natural faith; make these your last words.
te.lib:h-at-amana: Praise be to Allah who fed us, gave us drink, sufficed us and sheltered us; how many have none to suffice them and none to shelter them.
te.lib:h-rabbana-atina: O Allah, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
te.lib:h-huda-tuqa: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and self-sufficiency.
te.lib:h-ighfir-warhamni: Say: “O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me well-being and provide for me” (and he gathered his fingers except the thumb), for these gather for you your world and your Hereafter.
te.lib:h-musarrif-qulub: O Allah, Turner of hearts, turn our hearts to Your obedience.
te.lib:h-jahd-bala: Seek refuge in Allah from the strain of affliction, from being overtaken by misery, from an evil decree, and from the gloating of enemies.
te.lib:h-aslih-dini: O Allah, set right for me my religion which is the safeguard of my affairs, set right for me my world in which is my living, set right for me my Hereafter to which is my return; make life an increase for me in every good, and make death a rest for me from every evil.
te.lib:h-ajz-kasal: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from inability and laziness, from cowardice and decrepitude, and from miserliness; I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave and from the trials of life and death.
te.lib:h-zalamtu-nafsi: Say: “O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins but You; so forgive me with forgiveness from You and have mercy on me; You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.”
te.lib:h-sharr-ghina-faqr: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness and decrepitude, from sin and debt, from the trial of the grave and its punishment, from the trial of the Fire and its punishment, and from the evil of the trial of wealth; and I seek refuge in You from the trial of poverty.
te.lib:h-munkarat-akhlaq: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from bad character, bad deeds and bad desires.
te.lib:h-sharr-sami: Say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing, the evil of my sight, the evil of my tongue, the evil of my heart and the evil of my desire.”
te.lib:h-ju-khiyana: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is an evil bedfellow, and I seek refuge in You from betrayal, for it is an evil inner trait.
te.lib:h-sal-afiya: O ‘Abbas, uncle of the Messenger of Allah, ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter.
te.lib:h-dua-bi-zahr-ghayb: The supplication of a Muslim for his brother in his absence is answered: at his head is an angel; whenever he prays for good for his brother, the angel says: “Amen, and for you the same.”
te.lib:h-jazak-allah: Whoever is done a favour and says to the one who did it, “May Allah reward you with good”, has done his utmost in praise.
te.lib:h-la-tadu-ala-anfusikum: Do not pray against yourselves, do not pray against your children and do not pray against your wealth, lest it coincide with an hour in which Allah is asked and He answers you.
te.lib:h-dua-istijaba: There is no Muslim on earth who calls upon Allah with a supplication but Allah gives it to him, or turns away from him an equal evil, as long as he does not pray for sin or for cutting ties of kinship.
te.lib:h-shibr-ard: Whoever takes a hand-span of land unjustly, it will be hung around his neck from seven earths.
te.lib:h-ma-bayna-lahyayh: Whoever guarantees me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee him Paradise.
te.lib:h-kalima-la-yatabayyan: A servant may say a word without thinking about it, and because of it he slips into the Fire further than the distance between the east and the west.
te.lib:h-thumma-istaqim: Say: “My Lord is Allah”, then be steadfast.
te.lib:h-amsik-lisanak: Hold your tongue, let your home suffice you, and weep over your sins.
te.lib:h-dimaukum-haram: Your blood, your wealth and your honour are sacred to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this land of yours. Have I not conveyed?
te.lib:h-azfar-nuhas: When I was taken up, I passed by people with nails of copper scratching their faces and chests. I said: “Who are these, Jibril?” He said: “These are those who eat the flesh of people and attack their honour.”
te.lib:h-radd-an-ird: Whoever defends the honour of his brother, Allah will turn the Fire away from his face on the Day of Resurrection.
te.lib:h-adh: Shall I tell you what al-‘adh is? It is tale-bearing, the talk carried between people.
te.lib:h-dhu-wajhayn: You will find people like mines; the best of them before Islam are the best in Islam if they understand; and you will find the worst of people to be the two-faced, who comes to these with one face and to those with another.
te.lib:h-tahallum: Whoever claims a dream he did not see will be made to tie two barley grains together and will not manage; whoever listens to the talk of people who dislike that, molten lead will be poured into his ears on the Day of Resurrection.
te.lib:h-kafa-kadhiban: It is enough of a lie for a person to relate everything he hears.
te.lib:h-mutashabbi: The one who pretends to have what he was not given is like one wearing two garments of falsehood.
te.lib:h-la-yanbaghi-lianan: It is not fitting for a truthful person to be one who curses much.
te.lib:h-sibab-fusuq: Insulting a Muslim is wickedness, and fighting him is disbelief.
te.lib:h-la-tasubbu-amwat: Do not insult the dead, for they have reached what they sent ahead.
te.lib:h-yuta-ilayh: Whoever loves to be moved away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise, let death come to him while he believes in Allah and the Last Day, and let him treat people the way he loves to be treated.
te.lib:h-la-tabaghadu: Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn your backs on one another and do not cut ties; be, servants of Allah, brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim to shun his brother for more than three days.
te.lib:h-awrat-al-muslimin: If you pursue the faults of Muslims, you will corrupt them, or nearly corrupt them.
te.lib:h-yahqir: It is enough evil for a person to look down on his Muslim brother.
te.lib:h-man-ghashshana: Why did you not put it on top of the food so people could see it? Whoever cheats is not of us.
te.lib:h-khabbaba: Whoever turns a man's wife against him, or his servant, is not of us.
te.lib:h-liwa-ghadir: Every betrayer will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection; it will be said: “This is the betrayal of so-and-so.”
te.lib:h-ajir-ajrah: Allah said: “Three I will be the opponent of on the Day of Resurrection: a man who gave his word by Me and then betrayed it, a man who sold a free person and ate his price, and a man who hired a worker, took full work from him and did not give him his wage.”
te.lib:h-halaka-nas: When a man says “The people are ruined”, he is the most ruined of them.
te.lib:h-tahrish: Satan has despaired of being worshipped by those who pray in the Arabian Peninsula, but not of stirring them up against one another.
te.lib:h-la-yatanaja: When you are three, two should not converse privately apart from the third until you mingle with people, because that would grieve him.
te.lib:h-hirra: A woman was punished because of a cat she confined until it died, and she entered the Fire for it: she neither fed it nor gave it water while she confined it, nor let it eat from the creatures of the earth.
te.lib:h-yuadhdhibuna-nas: Allah punishes those who torment people in this world.
te.lib:h-aghna-shuraka: Allah says: “I am the most free of partners from association; whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I leave him and his association.”
te.lib:h-sammaa: Whoever seeks to be heard of, Allah will make him heard of; and whoever shows off, Allah will show him off.
te.lib:h-zina-ayn: The son of Adam's share of zina is written for him and he will meet it without doubt: the zina of the eyes is looking, the zina of the ears is listening, the zina of the tongue is speech, the zina of the hand is grasping, the zina of the foot is stepping; the heart yearns and desires, and the private part confirms it or denies it.
te.lib:h-haqq-tariq: Lowering the gaze, refraining from harm, returning greetings, enjoining good and forbidding evil.
te.lib:h-darb-khudud: He is not of us who strikes his cheeks, tears his garments and calls with the call of the age of ignorance.
te.lib:h-yujibuni-fal: There is no contagion and no evil omen, and I like optimism.
te.lib:h-iqtataa-haqq: Whoever takes the right of a Muslim by his oath, Allah has made the Fire obligatory for him and forbidden him Paradise.
te.lib:h-kabair: The major sins are: associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, killing a soul, and the false oath.
te.lib:h-fa-ti-khayr: If you swear an oath and then see something better than it, do what is better and make expiation for your oath.
te.lib:h-la-tasubbi-humma: Do not curse fever, for it removes the sins of the children of Adam as the bellows remove the impurities of iron.
te.lib:h-fuhsh-haya: Obscenity is not in anything except that it disfigures it, and modesty is not in anything except that it adorns it.
te.lib:h-laqisat-nafsi: None of you should say “My soul has become wicked”; let him say “My soul is out of sorts.”
te.lib:h-yazim-masala: When one of you supplicates, let him be resolute in asking and not say “O Allah, if You will, give me”, for none can compel Him.
te.lib:h-ihdad: It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn a deceased person for more than three nights, except for a husband: four months and ten days.
te.lib:h-la-yakhtub: Let none of you sell over the sale of another, nor propose marriage over the proposal of his brother, unless he gives him permission.
te.lib:h-qila-wa-qal: Allah is pleased with three things for you and dislikes three things for you: He is pleased that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and that you hold together to the rope of Allah and do not split; and He dislikes for you gossip, excessive questioning and wasting wealth.
te.lib:h-ahsibu: If one of you must praise, let him say: “I consider him so-and-so, and Allah is his reckoner” if he thinks him so, and not declare anyone pure before Allah.
te.lib:h-taun: If you hear of it (the plague) in a land, do not go to it; and if it occurs in a land where you are, do not leave it fleeing from it.
te.lib:h-wussida-amr: When the matter is entrusted to those not fit for it, then wait for the Hour.
te.lib:h-idha-lam-tastahi: Among what people have received of the words of the earlier prophethood: if you feel no shame, do as you wish.
te.lib:h-liqa-allah: When the believer is given glad tidings of Allah's mercy, His pleasure and His Paradise, he loves to meet Allah and Allah loves to meet him.
te.lib:h-majra-dam: Satan flows in the son of Adam as blood flows, and I feared he might cast evil into your hearts.
te.lib:h-ijtihad-ajran: When a judge rules, strives hard and is right, he has two rewards; and if he rules, strives hard and errs, he has one reward.
te.lib:h-yughan: A cloud comes over my heart, and I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times a day.
te.lib:h-law-lam-tudhnibu: By the One in whose hand is my soul, if you did not sin, Allah would take you away and bring a people who sin and then seek Allah's forgiveness, and He would forgive them.
te.lib:h-rabbi-ighfir-li: My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance; You are the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.
te.lib:h-astaghfiru-hayy: Whoever says “I seek the forgiveness of Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, and I turn to Him in repentance”, his sins are forgiven even if he had fled from the battle.
te.lib:h-ma-la-ayn-raat: Allah said: “I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to a human heart.”
te.lib:h-tasihhu-la-tasqamu: When the people of Paradise enter it, a caller calls out: “You will live and never die, you will be healthy and never fall ill, you will be young and never grow old, and you will enjoy and never suffer hardship.”
te.lib:h-hamma-bi-hasana: Allah has written good and bad deeds. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, Allah writes it with Him as a full good deed; if he intends it and does it, Allah writes it as ten good deeds up to seven hundred times and many more. If he intends a bad deed and does not do it, Allah writes it as a full good deed; and if he does it, Allah writes it as a single bad deed.
te.lib:h-afrah-bi-tawba: Allah is more delighted with the repentance of His servant than one of you who finds his camel after losing it in a desert land.
te.lib:h-ma-lam-yugharghir: Allah accepts the repentance of a servant as long as he is not at his last breath.
te.lib:h-wadiyan-min-dhahab: If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would love to have two valleys; nothing fills his mouth but dust, and Allah turns to whoever repents.
te.lib:h-lillahi-ma-akhadh: To Allah belongs what He took and to Him belongs what He gave, and everything with Him has an appointed term; so let her be patient and hope for reward.
te.lib:h-safiyyuhu: Allah says: “My believing servant has no reward with Me, when I take his beloved from the people of the world and he endures it seeking reward, except Paradise.”
te.lib:h-ighfir-li-qawmi: O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know.
te.lib:h-rahima-musa: (When a man said the distribution was unjust:) Who would be just if Allah and His Messenger are not just? Then he said: May Allah have mercy on Musa; he was harmed with more than this and was patient.
te.lib:h-ajjala-uquba: When Allah wants good for His servant, He hastens his punishment in this world; and when He wants evil for His servant, He withholds his sin from him until He meets him with it on the Day of Resurrection.
te.lib:h-bala-mumin: Trials continue to afflict the believing man and woman in themselves, their children and their wealth until they meet Allah with no sin upon them.
te.lib:h-athara: There will be after me favouritism and things you will disapprove of. They said: What do you command us? He said: Fulfil the right that is upon you, and ask Allah for the right that is yours.
te.lib:h-isbiru-hatta-talqawni: You will meet favouritism after me, so be patient until you meet me at the Basin.
te.lib:h-la-tatamannaw-aduww: O people, do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being; but when you meet them, be steadfast.
te.lib:h-tarkuhu-ma-la-yanih: Part of the excellence of a person's Islam is leaving what does not concern him.
te.lib:h-thalithuhuma: What do you think, Abu Bakr, of two whose third is Allah?
te.lib:h-bismillah-tawakkaltu: Whoever says, on leaving his house, “In the name of Allah, I rely on Allah, there is no might nor power except by Allah”, it is said to him: “You are sufficed and protected”, and Satan moves away from him.
te.lib:h-man-ada-li-waliyya: Allah said: “Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I declare war on him. My servant draws near to Me with nothing more beloved to Me than what I made obligatory on him, and My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him; and when I love him I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes and his foot with which he walks; if he asks Me I will surely give him, and if he seeks refuge in Me I will surely protect him.”
te.lib:h-shibran-dhiraa: When the servant draws near to Me a hand-span, I draw near to him a forearm's length; when he draws near to Me a forearm's length, I draw near to him an arm-span; and when he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.
te.lib:h-abdan-shakura: (When asked why he prayed until his feet swelled though he was forgiven:) Should I not love to be a grateful servant?
te.lib:h-huffat-janna: The Fire is veiled with desires, and Paradise is veiled with hardships.
te.lib:h-shirak-nalih: Paradise is nearer to one of you than the strap of his sandal, and so is the Fire.
te.lib:h-tala-umruhu: The best of people is the one whose life is long and whose deeds are good.
te.lib:h-firsin-shat: O Muslim women, let no neighbour belittle a gift to her neighbour, even the hoof of a sheep.
te.lib:h-yaghrisu-gharsan: No Muslim plants a plant but whatever is eaten from it is charity for him, whatever is stolen from it is charity for him, whatever wild animals eat from it is charity for him, whatever birds eat from it is charity for him, and whoever takes anything from it, it is charity for him.
te.lib:h-bima-tutiqun: Enough! Take on what you can bear; by Allah, Allah does not grow weary until you grow weary.
te.lib:h-yusalli-nashatahu: (Seeing a rope tied for support during long prayer:) Untie it; let one of you pray while he has energy, and when he tires, let him sleep.
te.lib:h-sanna-sunna: Whoever starts a good practice in Islam has its reward and the reward of those who act on it after him without anything lessened from their rewards; and whoever starts a bad practice in Islam bears its burden and the burden of those who act on it after him without anything lessened from their burdens.
te.lib:h-dalla-ala-khayr: Whoever guides to good has a reward like that of the one who does it.
te.lib:h-safina: The likeness of one who keeps to Allah's limits and one who transgresses them is like people who drew lots on a ship: some got the upper deck and some the lower. Those below, when they needed water, passed by those above and said: “If we made a hole in our share we would not trouble those above.” If they leave them to do what they want, all will perish; and if they stop them, they will be saved and all will be saved.
te.lib:h-kalimat-adl: The best jihad is a word of justice before a tyrannical ruler.
te.lib:h-akhadhu-ala-yadayh: When people see a wrongdoer and do not take him by the hand, Allah may soon cover them all with punishment from Him.
te.lib:h-tuaddunna-huquq: Rights will be rendered to their owners on the Day of Resurrection, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned sheep.
te.lib:h-fal-yatahallalhu: Whoever has wronged his brother in his honour or anything else, let him seek his pardon today, before there is neither dinar nor dirham; if he has good deeds, some will be taken in proportion to his wrong, and if he has no good deeds, some of the other's bad deeds will be taken and placed on him.
te.lib:h-illa-ddayn: (About the martyr's sins:) Yes, if you are patient, seeking reward, advancing and not retreating, except debt; Jibril told me that.
te.lib:h-alhanu-bi-hujjatih: I am only human, and you bring your disputes to me; some of you may be more eloquent in argument than others, and I judge according to what I hear. Whoever I judge to have something of his brother's right, I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire.
te.lib:h-bunyan: The believer to the believer is like a building, each part strengthening the other.
te.lib:h-akhu-al-muslim: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not wrong him nor abandon him. Whoever meets his brother's need, Allah meets his need; whoever relieves a Muslim of a distress, Allah relieves him of a distress of the Day of Resurrection; and whoever covers a Muslim, Allah covers him on the Day of Resurrection.
te.lib:h-taqwa-hahuna: The Muslim is the brother of the Muslim: he does not betray him, lie to him or abandon him. All of the Muslim is sacred to the Muslim: his honour, his wealth and his blood. Piety is here. It is enough evil for a person to look down on his Muslim brother.
te.lib:h-unsur-akhak: Help your brother whether he is a wrongdoer or wronged. A man said: I help him when he is wronged, but how do I help him when he is the wrongdoer? He said: You hold him back from wrongdoing; that is helping him.
te.lib:h-satara-abdan: No servant covers another servant in this world except that Allah will cover him on the Day of Resurrection.
te.lib:h-kullu-daif: Shall I not tell you of the people of Paradise? Every weak one, looked down upon, who if he swore by Allah, Allah would fulfil it. Shall I not tell you of the people of the Fire? Every harsh, greedy, arrogant one.
te.lib:h-khayrun-min-mil: (Of a poor man people disregarded, compared with a rich one they esteemed:) This one is better than an earthful of the likes of that one.
te.lib:h-ashath-aghbar: Many a dishevelled, dusty one, turned away from doors, if he swore by Allah, Allah would fulfil it.
te.lib:h-laallaka-aghdabtahum: Abu Bakr, perhaps you angered them? If you angered them, you have angered your Lord.
te.lib:h-kafil-yatim-lahu: The one who looks after an orphan, whether a relative or not, he and I will be like these two in Paradise.
te.lib:h-yataffaf: The poor one is not the one turned away by a date or two or a morsel or two; the poor one is the one who refrains from asking.
te.lib:h-jariyatayn: Whoever raises two girls until they reach maturity, he and I will come on the Day of Resurrection like this.
te.lib:h-bi-duafaikum: Are you given victory and provision except through your weak ones?
te.lib:h-haqq-zawja: (The wife's right is) that you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike the face, do not revile her, and do not leave her except within the house.
te.lib:h-dinar-ala-ahlik: A dinar you spend in Allah's cause, a dinar you spend to free a slave, a dinar you give in charity to a poor person, and a dinar you spend on your family: the greatest of them in reward is the one you spend on your family.
te.lib:h-yahbisa-qutah: It is enough of a sin for a person to withhold the sustenance of those he is responsible for.
te.lib:h-malakan: There is no day on which the servants wake but two angels descend; one says: “O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement”, and the other says: “O Allah, give the one who withholds ruin.”
te.lib:h-yastafif: The upper hand is better than the lower hand. Start with those you support. The best charity is from surplus. Whoever seeks to refrain from asking, Allah will keep him chaste; and whoever seeks self-sufficiency, Allah will make him self-sufficient.
te.lib:h-maraqa: When you cook a broth, add more water to it, then look to a household among your neighbours and give them some of it with kindness.
te.lib:h-khayr-ashab: The best of companions with Allah is the best of them to his companion, and the best of neighbours with Allah is the best of them to his neighbour.
te.lib:h-rahim-maqam: Allah created creation, and when He finished, the womb (kinship) stood and said: “This is the place of one who seeks refuge in You from being cut off.” He said: “Yes; are you not pleased that I join whoever joins you and cut off whoever cuts you?” It said: “Certainly.” He said: “That is yours.”
te.lib:h-abulluha: (Of a clan of his relatives who did not share his faith: they are not my allies; my ally is Allah and the righteous believers.) But they have a tie of kinship with me which I keep moist with its due.
te.lib:h-awsat-abwab: The father is the middle gate of Paradise; so if you wish, lose that gate, or keep it.
te.lib:h-yasubbu-aba-rajul: (Among the major sins is a man cursing his parents.) He curses a man's father, and the man curses his father; he curses his mother, and the man curses his mother.
te.lib:h-wudd-abih: The finest of righteousness is that a man keeps up ties with the loved ones of his father.
te.lib:h-kanat-wa-kanat: (Of Khadijah:) She was such and such, and I had children from her.
te.lib:h-tibta: Whoever visits a sick person or visits a brother for the sake of Allah, a caller calls out: “You are good, your walking is good, and you have taken a place in Paradise.”
te.lib:h-la-tusahib: Do not keep company except with a believer, and let none eat your food but the pious.
te.lib:h-arwah-junud: People are mines like mines of gold and silver; the best of them before Islam are the best in Islam if they understand. Souls are gathered troops: those that recognise one another become familiar, and those that do not recognise one another differ.
te.lib:h-halawat-iman: Three things, whoever has them finds the sweetness of faith: that Allah and His Messenger are dearer to him than all else; that he loves a person only for Allah; and that he hates to return to disbelief after Allah saved him from it as he hates to be thrown into the fire.
te.lib:h-mutahabbun: Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection: “Where are those who loved one another for My majesty? Today I will shade them in My shade on a day when there is no shade but Mine.”
te.lib:h-qurab-al-ard: Allah says: “Whoever comes with a good deed has ten like it or more; whoever comes with a bad deed, its recompense is one like it, or I forgive. Whoever draws near to Me a hand-span, I draw near to him a forearm; whoever draws near a forearm, I draw near an arm-span; whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running. And whoever meets Me with an earthful of sins without associating anything with Me, I meet him with its like in forgiveness.”
te.lib:h-arhamu-biibadihi: (Seeing a captive mother hold her baby to her chest:) Do you think this woman would throw her child into the fire? We said: No. He said: Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child.
te.lib:h-mia-rahma: Allah made mercy a hundred parts; He kept ninety-nine with Him and sent down one part to the earth; from that one part creatures show mercy to one another, so that the mare lifts its hoof away from its foal for fear of hurting it.
te.lib:h-law-yalamu-mumin: If the believer knew what punishment is with Allah, none would hope for His Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew what mercy is with Allah, none would despair of His Paradise.
te.lib:h-ma-al-faqr-akhsha: Rejoice and hope for what pleases you; by Allah, it is not poverty that I fear for you, but I fear that the world will be spread out for you as it was for those before you, and you will compete for it as they competed, and it will destroy you as it destroyed them.
te.lib:h-tais-abd-dinar: Wretched is the slave of the dinar, the dirham and fine clothes: if he is given he is pleased, and if he is not given he is displeased.
te.lib:h-mali-mali: The son of Adam says: “My wealth, my wealth!” Do you have, son of Adam, of your wealth anything but what you ate and used up, wore and wore out, or gave in charity and sent ahead?
te.lib:h-dhiban-jaian: Two hungry wolves let loose among sheep are not more destructive to them than a person's greed for wealth and status is to his religion.
te.lib:h-ka-rakib: What have I to do with the world? I am in the world only like a rider who took shade under a tree, then went on and left it.
te.lib:h-la-tulam-ala-kafaf: Son of Adam, if you give the surplus it is better for you, and if you hold it back it is worse for you; you are not blamed for having just enough, and start with those you support.
te.lib:h-ayshuhu-kafafan: Blessed is the one guided to Islam whose living is just sufficient and who is content.
te.lib:h-thuluth: A human fills no vessel worse than his stomach; a few morsels to keep his back straight are enough for the son of Adam; and if he must, then a third for his food, a third for his drink and a third for his breath.
te.lib:h-bi-sakhawat-nafs: Hakim, this wealth is green and sweet; whoever takes it with a generous soul is blessed in it, and whoever takes it with a greedy soul is not blessed in it and is like one who eats and is never full; and the upper hand is better than the lower hand.
te.lib:h-anzalaha-billah: Whoever is struck by need and takes it to people, his need will not be relieved; and whoever is struck by need and takes it to Allah, Allah will soon give him provision, sooner or later.
te.lib:h-tutimu-taam: (Which Islam is best?) That you feed people and give the greeting of peace to those you know and those you do not know.
te.lib:h-adl-tamra: Whoever gives in charity the equal of a date from good earnings, and Allah accepts only the good, Allah takes it with His right hand and raises it for its owner as one of you raises his foal, until it becomes like a mountain.
te.lib:h-la-hasad-illa: There is no envy except in two: a man to whom Allah gave the Qur'an and he stands with it through the night and day, and a man to whom Allah gave wealth and he spends it through the night and day.
te.lib:h-la-yatamanna-mawt: Let none of you wish for death, nor pray for it before it comes to him; when he dies his deeds stop, and the believer's life only increases him in good.
te.lib:h-husn-khuluq-saim: The believer, by his good character, reaches the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer at night.
te.lib:h-hilm-anah: You have two traits that Allah loves: forbearance and deliberateness.
te.lib:h-yuhram-rifq: Whoever is deprived of gentleness is deprived of all good.
te.lib:h-hayyin-layyin: Shall I not tell you who is forbidden to the Fire, or to whom the Fire is forbidden? Every one who is close to people, gentle, easy-going and easy to deal with.
te.lib:h-munaffirin: O people, among you are those who drive people away; whoever of you leads the people, let him be brief, for behind him are the old, the young and those with needs.
te.lib:h-man-waliya: O Allah, whoever is given charge of any affair of my nation and is harsh with them, be harsh with him; and whoever is given charge of any affair of my nation and is gentle with them, be gentle with him.
te.lib:h-ihtajaba: Whoever Allah gives charge of any affair of the Muslims and screens himself from their needs, their want and their poverty, Allah will screen Himself from his need, his want and his poverty on the Day of Resurrection.
te.lib:h-muqsitun: The just will be with Allah on pulpits of light at the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both His hands are right: those who are just in their judgement, with their families and in whatever they are given charge of.
te.lib:h-la-taa-fi-masiya: The Muslim must listen and obey in what he likes and dislikes, unless he is commanded to disobey; if he is commanded to disobey, there is no listening and no obedience.
te.lib:h-la-tasal-imara: Do not ask for leadership; if you are given it without asking you will be helped in it, and if you are given it because you asked you will be left to it.
te.lib:h-innaha-amana: Abu Dharr, you are weak, and it is a trust; on the Day of Resurrection it is disgrace and regret, except for whoever takes it rightfully and fulfils what is due in it.
te.lib:h-bitanatan: Allah has not sent any prophet nor appointed any successor except that he has two close circles: one that commands him to good and urges him to it, and one that commands him to evil and urges him to it; and the protected one is whom Allah protects.
